analysis.title: Mohawk Industries Inc. (MHK): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: MHK reported 3Q26 adj. EPS of $2.72 vs GS estimate $2.62 and FactSet consensus $2.58. The beat came from lower interest expense (+$0.06) and revenue about +1% vs GS -1% estimate (+$0.04).
Adj. EBIT margin was 7.2%, 26bps below the GS model (-$0.09). Offsets were a lower share count (+$0.04), one-time items (+$0.03) and taxes (+$0.02).
Sales grew about 4% from price/mix, offset by an equal decline in volumes, in line with softer housing and consumer confidence. Operating cash flow (CFO) was $471mn.
4Q26 guide: low-single-digit revenue growth vs GS model of -1.6%. Mid-point adj. EPS of $1.40 is below GS ($1.67) and consensus ($1.64).
Flooring North America sales rose 1.4% YOY (about flat adjusted), with one extra selling day adding 2pts, vs GS -2.4%. Adj. EBIT margin was 8.1%, 38bps above GS and up 84bps YOY.
Global Ceramic sales grew 2.2% YOY (+1% adjusted) vs GS -1.6%. Adj. EBIT margin was 6.5%, 19bps below GS and down 162bps YOY on inflation and lost operating leverage.
Flooring ROW sales fell 1.2% (-2% adjusted) vs GS +3.3%. Adj. EBIT margin was 9.3%, 54bps below GS and up 99bps YOY.
Net debt/EBITDA was 0.7x, vs 0.8x in 2Q26 and 1.1x a year ago, with $817mn of cash. $261mn of stock was repurchased in 3Q and $34mn more in 4Q, completing the prior authorization.

A separate release set a leverage target of up to 2x adj. EBITDA, annual capex of about $375mn for the next several years, and a new $500mn repurchase authorization. It also stressed organic growth and small bolt-on M&A.
GS sees potential for upward EPS revisions as these initiatives are executed. Second-half buybacks have cut the share count by about 4%, adding $0.04+ to EPS.
GS rates MHK Buy with a $153 12-month target based on 7.1x Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA. The stock closed at $129.99, implying 17.7% upside.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 adj. EPS beat on lower interest expense and better revenue. New capital allocation targets and buybacks could drive upward EPS revisions, though the 4Q EPS guide is below consensus.

risk_factors: Delays or inability to deliver on strategic initiatives.
Greater competition if peers seek to gain share.
Greater risk or uncertainty around international production and sales.
Higher raw material costs that cannot be passed through.
Moderating housing demand and consumer confidence, rising rates for commercial end-markets, and inflationary headwinds.
geopolitical: GS will ask on the call about demand in international markets given the geopolitical backdrop and about the impact of higher global energy prices.
